newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields up, govt issues wages warning.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields up, govt issues wages warning.

text.p: *Australian bond yields touched their highest level in a week, fuelled by comments from the government which raised concerns over future wages growth.
*U.S. retail sales for June due later on Tuesday.
Australian bond yields touched their highest level in a week just before the close fuelled by comments by a government minister, which raised concerns over future wages growth.

The market had already been showing a mildly negative tone in the aftermath of Monday's weaker U.S. Treasury market, and as it unwound some of the bullishness last week which followed a weaker than expected employment report.
Australian Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith said some demands for wage increases would push wages growth above the RBA targets and would not be good for interest rates.

"It was probably a bit of sabre rattling over one or two specific deals rather than wages in general," said UBS Australia's chief economist Stephen Roberts, but added that the timing of the comments came when the market was already showing some signs of vulberability.
The market is currently suffering from a dearth of key economic data and has to wait until next week before it sees the second quarter inflation and wages reports.
Continued weakness in the Australian dollar, which struck a fresh 18-month low today, was also weighing slightly on the short end, but not sufficiently to rule out a policy easing.

While the local dollar is weakening against the U.S. dollar, it is still holding above its five-year average in trade weighted terms of 54.0 points and is still above the recent TWI low of 49.0 seen in 1995, said UBS's Roberts, who is still anticipating an easing in current official 5.5 percent rate.
The immediate focus for the local market is on U.S. June retail sales due later on Tuesday, which is forecast to show a modest 0.2 percent rebound after three consecutive montly falls.

The local market's weaker tone saw it underperform against the dollar bloc and yields were near enough back to levels seen prior to last week's weaker than expected employment report, which had sparked off further thoughts of a policy easing.
